submission.justification: Module-D1 gives the most light (53.6 PE/MeV at 30%), but 30% of D1 modules failed thermal cycling because the light-guide bond cracks. The hard limit is 5%, and failed modules cannot be replaced once the cryostat is filled, so D1 is ruled out. Of the two designs that pass, D2 (2% failures) collects more light than D3 (0.5% failures) at every coverage simulated: 36.2 vs 24.7 PE/MeV at 30%. Light collection rises with coverage (27.1 PE/MeV for D2 at 20%, 36.2 at 30%), so the 30% maximum is best. The 2026-01-20 meeting notes confirm there are enough cabling feedthroughs for 30% coverage. Caveat: D2's 2% failure rate comes from one batch of 40 modules (about 1 failure). That passes, but with limited statistical margin below 5%.

requirements.evidence: D2 at 30% gives 36.2 PE/MeV, the highest among designs that pass thermal cycling (D3 gives 24.7 at 30%). D1 (53.6) is excluded.

requirements.requirement: Module is one of the three candidate designs
requirements.evidence: Module-D2 (wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout) is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: At most 5% failures after 20 thermal cycles
requirements.evidence: D2: 2% failed in a batch of 40 modules (thermal_cycling_tests.md and query). Limited statistics: about 1 failure out of 40.
30% chosen; the meeting notes confirm enough feedthroughs for up to 30%.
